newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Aluminum-Argentina's Aluar plans bonds to expand.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum-Argentina's Aluar plans bonds to expand.

text.p: Aluminio Argentino (Aluar) is studying a big bond issue after approving a $300 million expansion to boost annual refined aluminum output by 72,000 tonnes to 258,000 tonnes, a top official said.
Aluar's administration manager Gregorio Krauchik said the firm would seek about a third of the money from international organizations such as Eximbank.
"The other two-thirds of the money we are going to try and obtain with some sort of bond, although this is still under analysis," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Krauchik said any bond would be placed abroad, and that any issue would be supported by Aluar's position as an exporter.

Aluar studied the expansion for two years before finally reaching agreements with natural gas producers to supply its plant in Puerto Madryn, in far southern Argentina. The firm will acquire a new 120 MW gas-fired combined cycle generator.
All the extra output will go for export.
"We'll export a bit more to Japan, to other countries in the Far East. And we will try to develop new markets like the United States with new products like aluminum alloys," Krauchik said.
Aluar exports about two-thirds of its current output, particularly to Japan and Chile.

Krauchik said the price of energy and the technology for the expansion supplied by France's Aluminium Pechiney should ensure that the extra output is competitive. Krauchik was also optimistic for aluminum's price outlook.
"We have the sensation that the industry will not permit low prices for any length of time," he said.
It has been a grim year for aluminum prices and demand, but there are hopes that offtake will strengthen in 1997 and swab up extra metal set to hit the world market.
Aluar expects its expansion to be completed by July 1999.
The firm imports its raw material, alumina, from Brazil, the Caribbean, and occasionally from Australia. Its sole supplier is presently the Aluminum Company of America (Alcoa) .
While talks over the cost of extra energy long delayed a decision over the expansion, Aluar already owns its own 120-MW power station and bought a the 448-MW Futaleufu hydroelectric dam in 1995.
The company is controlled by Argentina's Madanes family.
